references.text: The prohibition against making carved images and cast images is given in the Ten Commandments, which forms the basis for the curse in Deuteronomy 27:15
The prohibition against making cast gods is repeated here, emphasizing the seriousness of creating idol images
The prohibition against turning to idols and making cast god-images confirms that this is an abominable act to the Lord
The prohibition against setting up carved images or pillars emphasizes the Lord's hatred of idolatry
The warning against making carved images in any form elaborates on what is forbidden and abhorrent to the Lord
The repetition of the commandment against carved images in Deuteronomy shows the connection with the curse
The prophet Isaiah condemns those who make carved images and calls it useless and shameful
Jeremiah describes cast images as falsehood and the work of a craftsman, having no spirit within them
Habakkuk condemns those who make carved and cast images and calls them silent idols
Paul speaks against thinking that the deity can be compared to images made by human art and thought
